official.description: This scholarship helps international students who are intending to study for a Bachelor's degree to join Te Herenga Waka - Victoria University of Wellington's international student community. It is a partial fee-based scholarship that will go towards tuition fees for one year of study, designed for new international students who are entering their first year of a Bachelor's degree programme and studying full-time on campus.
official.program_type: Partial fee-based scholarship for new international undergraduate students
official.english_requirement: The scholarship page sets no separate English requirement; English ability is met through programme admission. VUW's published standard undergraduate English requirement is IELTS (Academic) overall 6.0 with no band lower than 5.5, TOEFL iBT total 80, PTE 50 with a Communication score no lower than 42, or Duolingo English Test 105 with no band less than 95; Victoria's own EAP final scores of 4, 4, 4, 3 also meet it.

applicant_utility.summary: There is nothing to submit for this scholarship beyond your programme application: VUW assesses eligibility automatically and names the award in the Offer of Place, so your real deadline is the programme deadline (8 December for Trimester 1, 1 May for Trimester 2, 1 September for Trimester 3 for international applicants). The NZ$15,000 comes off your tuition invoice upfront for your first year only, so budget for living costs, insurance and visa costs yourself, and for any tuition above $15,000. Apply early even though applications are accepted at any time, because late applications are handled case by case and you still need time for a student visa and accommodation.
applicant_utility.best_fit: New international school-leavers or first-degree students paying full international fees who want a fee discount at VUW without writing a scholarship essay.
application_readiness_checklist: Apply for the Bachelor's programme through VUW's international application well before the trimester deadline for your intake
Meet the published standard undergraduate English requirement (or complete Victoria's EAP or Foundation Studies, which keep you eligible)
Check your Offer of Place for the scholarship before accepting and paying, so you know the reduced tuition amount
Enrol in first-year courses, since the award is only formalised once you enrol
If your plans shift, request deferral approval before the intake, and only to another intake in the same calendar year
common_rejection_risks: Being a returning student: current VUW students are not eligible, so second-year entry does not qualify
Having credit transfer, advanced standing or recognition of prior learning from a previous qualification
Government sponsorship from your home country or the New Zealand Government
Applying as a Study Abroad, Exchange or Twinning student from an overseas partner university
Holding Australian or New Zealand citizenship, permanent residency, a resident visa or a domestic-status diplomatic visa
Accepting an offer but not enrolling in first-year courses, since the scholarship is only formally awarded on enrolment
Withdrawing after the award, which can trigger repayment of some or all of the value at the University's discretion
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs, accommodation, health insurance, student visa and travel costs, and any tuition fees above the NZ$15,000 credit in the first year; the scholarship covers tuition fees only.
document_audit: No scholarship-specific documents exist - do not wait for a scholarship form or reference; your programme application is the application
The scholarship will not appear on your academic transcript, so keep the Offer of Place as your evidence
If your fee or residency status changes to domestic before the credit is applied, the scholarship is withdrawn, so keep your fee status documentation consistent with your application
alerts: Established in August 2025, combining and replacing the Tongarewa International Scholarship, the Latin American Academic Achievement Scholarship, the International Alumni Fees Waiver and the New Zealand International School-Leaver Grant, so advice about those older awards no longer applies
Only one scholarship is formally awarded per student even if you hold several Offers of Place from multiple programmes
Deferral is limited to another intake in the same calendar year - you cannot defer into the next year
It is a partial award, not full funding; treat the NZ$15,000 as a first-year tuition discount when planning your budget
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit one international application for the Bachelor's programme; Admissions assesses scholarship eligibility with the application and issues the Offer of Place stating the award, which is then credited to tuition when you enrol.

official.description: The Tulī Takes Flight scholarship is part of the gesture of goodwill and reconciliation to Aotearoa Pacific families and communities that followed the Government's 2021 apology for the Dawn Raids, acknowledging the ongoing importance of education for Aotearoa Pacific families and communities. It is intended to support Pacific people to reach their potential by reducing some of the financial barriers towards study or training, with scholarships for both vocational and academic study and training in Aotearoa.

applicant_utility.summary: Tulī Takes Flight is the Ministry of Education's flagship Pacific scholarship, worth $12,500 a year for vocational and undergraduate study and $17,500 a year at postgraduate level, and it can run for up to three years. The 2027 round closed at 11.59pm on 30 September 2026 with outcomes emailed by 18 March 2027, so the practical move now is to prepare documents and enrolment for the next round, which has historically opened in late August/September. Awards cover course costs including tuition, materials and equipment, plus help with living costs such as accommodation, transport and childcare, but you must be enrolled or enrolling in full-time study to apply.
applicant_utility.best_fit: New Zealand citizens or permanent residents of indigenous Pacific heritage entering or continuing full-time tertiary or vocational study in New Zealand, including first-year school leavers and experienced Pacific workers changing careers.
